items.title: Fix DatePicker Day.js bug in Ant Design example
items.body:
Bootstrapping the Ant Design example with `yarn create next-app --example with-ant-design with-ant-design-app`, then running `yarn dev`, I found that clicking on the DatePicker crashes the page, with console logs pointing to invalid calls to Moment.js functions. [Deploying the example with Vercel](https://vercel.com/import/project?template=https://github.com/zeit/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-ant-design) yields the same bug.

![nextjs-antd-example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5317080/81233373-91298200-8fc4-11ea-83cb-1d2db26bc0c0.gif)

Investigating, I saw that this example was attempting to use [antd-dayjs-webpack-plugin](https://github.com/ant-design/antd-dayjs-webpack-plugin) to use Day.js instead of Moment.js, but this plugin appears to be malfunctioning. I've removed the plugin and followed Ant Design's directions to [create a custom DatePicker that uses Day.js](https://ant.design/docs/react/replace-moment), and this fixes the bug, both locally and when [deploying with Vercel](https://vercel.com/import/project?template=https://github.com/tywmick/next.js/tree/ant-design-example-fix/examples/with-ant-design).

items.title: [Experimental] Implement optional catch all routes
items.body:
Allows defining a route as `/hello/[[...world]].js` that would match on `/hello`, `/hello/world` and `/hello/world/foo`. the `world` parameter on `/hello` would not exist on the `params`

Fixes: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/10488

following cases are invalid and will error during `next dev` and `next build`:

```
pages/[[...optional]].js
pages/index.js
```

```
pages/nested/[[...optional]].js
pages/nested.js
```

```
pages/[[...optional]].js
pages/[...catchall].js
```

```
pages/[[param]].js
```

`getSortedRoute` needs to be fed a list of all pages instead of dynamic only. That's because it needs to be able to check whether an optional route has an index route at its root. Dynamic pages are now filtered out of its result instead of its input.

Also of note is that the root of an optional catch-all `/hello/[[...world]].js` is accessible through both `/hello` and `/hello/`. This is also being tested for. Let me know if this behavior is not desired.

items.title: [Fast Refresh] Improve responsiveness on Windows
items.body:
The `eval-source-map` type is very slow to recompile on Windows, despite webpack's documentation.

This target is still preferable for macOS, where the reload speed is measurably faster than `inline-source-map` or `cheap-module-source-map`.

Due to this, **only Windows** will use `inline-source-map` for both Node.js and browser code.

I'd adjusted the code necessary to resolve these paths, and there should be no other test changes necessary if Windows tests pass.

---

Fixes #12797

items.title: [Experimental] Only consider files within plugins
items.body:
I have a plugin with a src folder structure following jest’s recommended practice of including a `__tests__` folder:

```
$ find src/
src/
src/document-html-props-server.ts
src/__tests__
src/__tests__/document-html-props-server.unit.ts
```

collect-plugins.ts [reads the src directory](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/960c18da53af89115c7e96dc8188646a51c53c15/packages/next/build/plugins/collect-plugins.ts#L65) and finds:
```js
[ '__tests__', 'document-html-props-server.ts' ]
```

…which it then [converts to](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/960c18da53af89115c7e96dc8188646a51c53c15/packages/next/build/plugins/collect-plugins.ts#L76-L80):
```js
[ '', 'document-html-props-server' ]
```

…and finally [outputs](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/960c18da53af89115c7e96dc8188646a51c53c15/packages/next/build/plugins/collect-plugins.ts#L90-L96):
```
Next.js Plugin: {my plugin} listed invalid middleware
```

This pull request makes collect-plugins.ts only consider files, so my __tests__ directory and its contents are ignored.

Use the jest-circus test runner
items.body:
Attempt at using the [`jest-circus` test runner](https://github.com/facebook/jest/tree/master/packages/jest-circus), which will become the [default in `jest` 27](https://github.com/facebook/jest/issues/6295#issuecomment-623080244). This allows for usage of [`jest.retryTimes`](https://jestjs.io/docs/en/jest-object#jestretrytimes) as a potential remedy against some of the test flakyness. 

Issues that came up so far:
- [x] `jest-circus` deprecates `jasmine` so all usage of `jasmine.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_INTERVAL` has to be replaced with `jest.setTimeout`.
- [x] looks like errors in `afterAll` now fail the test suite. There was a missing parameter [here](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/c239c746294495586fdf710266a7c3a78e09f199/test/integration/invalid-href/test/index.test.js#L146) and [here](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/c239c746294495586fdf710266a7c3a78e09f199/test/integration/custom-error/test/index.test.js#L42) and [here](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/c239c746294495586fdf710266a7c3a78e09f199/test/integration/custom-error/test/index.test.js#L65). It's supposed to be `afterAll(() => killApp(app))`.
- [x] [conformance suite](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/c239c746294495586fdf710266a7c3a78e09f199/test/integration/conformance/test/index.test.js#L18) tries to kill a server that isn't initialized.
- [x] EPERM errors in [create-next-app](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/c239c746294495586fdf710266a7c3a78e09f199/test/integration/create-next-app/index.test.js#L44) suite. Looks like `jest.setTimeout` only applies to `beforeAll` now if it's called in there, I moved it top-level in the suite. I also refactored these tests to be idempotent so that retries don't fail.

Just be aware: I've set `retryTimes` at 3 for all the suites. This shouldn't be problematic unless there are some tests that are not idempotent.

items.title: Add eslint-plugin-jest
items.body:
Linting the tests folder with [`eslint-plugin-jest`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/eslint-plugin-jest) to catch some common errors early on.

```json
    {
      "files": ["test/**/*.test.js"],
      "extends": ["plugin:jest/recommended"],
      "rules": {
        "jest/expect-expect": "off",
        "jest/no-disabled-tests": "off",
        "jest/no-try-expect": "off"
      }
    },
```

Problems that needed to be fixed before the plugin is enabled:
- [x] `expect` call without corresponding matcher: `expect($('.abc').length === 1)` will never throw, it needs to be written as `expect($('.abc').length === 1).toBe(true)` or better `expect($('.abc')).toHaveLength(1)`.
- [x] regression after fixing ☝️  in `integration/config`: ~is build id supposed to be `'-'` or `'development'`?~ [Did some forensics](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/4828#issuecomment-407435004), it's supposed to be `development` now.
- [x] regression after fixing ☝️ in `integration/config`: behavior of module-only package seems to be unexpected. Is the test out of date or is this a regression? https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/6256 @Timer it appears that with `'main', 'module'` as mainfields, webpack always resolves to `module/index.js` if it exists, even if `main` is not specified in package.json. ~Probably not an easy fix but it seems like this test never worked as intended. With this assumption, I will skip it for know.~ It's expected behavior, the fixture was wrong, this never got caught because of the missing expectation. Fixed the fixture to make the test pass
- [x] duplicate `describe` or `test` titles
- [x] replace commented out test with skipped test
- [x] duplicate `describe` or `test` titles in `integration/file-serving`: these seem to be duplicated tests, needs investigation: ignored those for now in this file. It can be cleaned up later if necessary

items.title: Add example: with-mux-video

labels.name: examples
labels.description: Issue was opened via the examples template.

items.body:
This example uses [Mux video](https://mux.com).

This is basically a [Streamable](https://streamable.com/) clone backed by NextJS and Mux. Here's the workflow:

1. User clicks a button
1. User uploads a video
1. Video is ready for playback at a unique URL

The features of Next.js this uses, which I think are cool:

* [SWR hook](https://swr.now.sh/) - dynamically changing the `refreshInterval` depending on if the client should be polling for updates or not
* `/pages/api` routes - a couple endpoints for making authenticated requests to the Mux API
* environment variables (`.env.example` file included) for authenticating requests to Mux
* [Dynamic client side routes](https://nextjs.org/learn/basics/dynamic-routes/page-path-external-data): this app uses `/pages/upload/[id].js`
* Dynamic api routes: this app uses `/pages/api/upload/[id].js`

Here's a deploy preview of the app https://with-mux-video.now.sh/

Questions:

* What is the best way to point users down the path of specifying environment variables?

+import ThemedStyleSheet from 'react-with-styles/lib/ThemedStyleSheet'

items.title: Example: Static Generation of local Apollo GraphQL schema

labels.name: examples
labels.description: Issue was opened via the examples template.

items.body:
## What

An example to show how you can create a static generated build of Next.js (using the new `getStaticProps` and `getStaticPaths` functions) with data fetched from a local GraphQL schema. The same schema is used to host a GraphQL endpoint using the API Route `/api/graphql`.

## Why

I was setting up a static hosted website whereby data is stored in a set of local JSON files (pulled from a backend server at build time). I wanted to consume the content using the developer benefits that GraphQL provides and using a consistent interface the GraphQL API consumers would be using.

Within my page components I initially made GraphQL `fetch` calls to the locally running `/api/graphql` endpoint which worked well with `npm run dev`, however when it came to `npm run build` that endpoint was inaccessible (I tried both VERCEL_URL and localhost:3000) - which is now understandable given I read further the "[Write server-side code directly](https://nextjs.org/docs/basic-features/data-fetching#write-server-side-code-directly)" documentation.

This example may or may not be useful for others so please feel free to close, but I thought I would contribute incase it assisted others.

## Related Discussions

It looks as though this PR may help with some of the following discussions:
  - https://github.com/zeit/next.js/discussions/12785
  - https://github.com/zeit/next.js/discussions/10946
  - https://github.com/zeit/next.js/discussions/12182
  - https://github.com/zeit/next.js/discussions/11285

## Related Examples

The end solution for this PR was a combination of web discussions and seeing the `api-routes-graphql` example. Perhaps this PR should just update that example to use the new methods? Or maybe it is worth having both?
- https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/examples/examples/api-routes-graphql

This is also similar to this example, although that example has more code in order to provide isomorphic Apollo Client for client side code use.
- https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/canary/examples/api-routes-apollo-server-and-client

## Errors Recieved
I've included the below errors as they are the ones I faced when figuring out the end solution. These may just help with SEO for others googling the same issue.

### Error when trying to use localhost:3000
```
> Build error occurred
{ FetchError: request to http://localhost:3000/api/graphql failed, reason: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000
    at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/vercel/7cf60e2b/.next/serverless/pages/content.js:1999:147829)
    at ClientRequest.emit (events.js:198:13)
    at Socket.socketErrorListener (_http_client.js:401:9)
    at Socket.emit (events.js:198:13)
    at emitErrorNT (internal/streams/destroy.js:91:8)
    at emitErrorAndCloseNT (internal/streams/destroy.js:59:3)
    at process._tickCallback (internal/process/next_tick.js:63:19) type: 'system', errno: 'ECONNREFUSED', code: 'ECONNREFUSED' }
```

### Error when trying to use VERCEL_URL
```
> Build error occurred
{ FetchError: invalid json response body at https://vercel.com/login?next=%2Fdeployments%2Fprojectnamehere.now.sh%3Fhost%3Dprojectnamehere.now.sh%26redirect%3D1%26section%3D reason: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0
    at /vercel/3d91c11/node_modules/next/dist/compiled/node-fetch/index.js:1:133590
    at process._tickCallback (internal/process/next_tick.js:68:7) type: 'invalid-json' }
```
